From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0500
Subject: Proposal: transoceanic demo rota + DST offset contingency

Hi all —

Thanks again for being flexible while we lock a slot that works for execs across US / EU / APAC. To avoid repeatedly rescheduling around DST transitions (coming Mar 2027 and Oct 2027) and to reduce late-night burden on APAC execs, I put together a rotating weekly demo "rota" so the hard hours rotate among us rather than always landing on the same region. Attached is a quick spreadsheet with proposed weeks and local times.

High-level proposal (week-by-week rotation):
- Week A (Americas lead): 09:00 PT / 12:00 ET / 17:00 CET / 01:00 JST (next day) — good for US/EU execs; APAC joins late evening
- Week B (EMEA lead): 08:30 GMT / 10:30 CET / 05:30 ET / 14:30 JST — better for EMEA, acceptable for US early morning
- Week C (APAC lead): 09:00 JST / 01:00 CET / 20:00 ET (prev day) — APAC-friendly, US evening

Notes:
- Times above are in local clocks; the rota spreadsheet includes UTC times and explicit examples for the two DST carve points (Mar and Oct 2027) so we know how the offsets will change.
- For weeks with an exec-only ask (C-level), we propose an "exec-only" 30-minute slot + separate engineer deep-dive at a different time so product/infra people aren't on late.
- If an exec absolutely cannot take the late slot on their week, the fallback is: record + 15-min post-demo sync with smaller overlap participants, or swap that week with the next week's lead.

Ask: please review the attached rota and reply with up to two absolute no-go windows for your exec(s) in Q1 2027 (Jan–Mar). If everyone is OK, I'll publish a draft calendar with alternating invites and a short blurb explaining the rotation.

Thanks — appreciate the patience here,
Olga
Olga Petrov
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com
(Attachment: rotating_demo_rota_v2.xlsx)

Thanks Olga — this looks thoughtful. Two quick notes from our side:

1) Our CTO is travel-heavy in Jan; absolute no-go weeks for him are the week of Jan 11 and Jan 25 (he's in the US those weeks).
2) The Mar 2027 DST shift is a pain point — could you add a summary row in the sheet that shows concrete local times for the first three demo dates (so our ops team can sanity-check invites)?

Also, for APAC folks, if the proposed Week A would land at 01:00 JST, that's borderline but doable; we'd appreciate an explicit "record + condensed follow-up" checkbox in the event invite for those weeks.

Best,
Suzanne Hough
Director, Partnerships — Acme Analytics
(suzanne.hough@acme-analytics.com)

Appreciate the draft, Olga. A couple of operational clarifications from platform-side:

- Our recommendation is to publish invites in UTC and include 3 pinned local-times in the event description for the first three instances (this avoids mail-client conversion errors during DST flips).
- For exec rotations, propose a 6-week cycle (A, B, C, A, B, C) rather than weekly to minimize frequent odd hours for on-call engineers. That keeps each region doing the late-night slot roughly twice a quarter.
- If an exec swap happens last-minute, we can offer a 10-minute live "handoff call" (recorded) right after the demo so the absent exec can get a concise summary.

I'll update the spreadsheet with a cycle column and add a small examples tab that lists local times for the first six demo dates spanning Jan–Mar 2027.

—Karthik
